newsitem.title: USA: Calif utilities seek FERC workshop on deregulation.
newsitem.headline: Calif utilities seek FERC workshop on deregulation.

text.p: California's three investor-owned utilities have asked the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to convene a technical workshop on market power issues raised by deregulation of the industry.
An initial workshop was held Jan 17, but the utilities feel they need more guidance, especially on contracts governing "must-run" generating units.
The utilities are Edison International's Southern California Edison Co, PG&E's Pacific Gas & Electric Co and Enova Corp's San Diego Gas & Electric Co.
They have been directed to have filings ready for FERC by March 31, and are seeking a second technical workshop for Feb 10.
The primary reason for the workshop is to examine ways to minimize the market power of generating units which will have to run to maintain reliability in certain regions, an Edison spokeswoman said.

Edison, which plans to sell off all of its fossil-fuel power plants, proposes establishing "call contracts" which would allow the independent system operator to order "must run" units to sell power into the power exchange at cost, said spokeswoman Gloria Quinn.

"When we do the filing on March 31, we want to make sure FERC has what they need to get approval (for the independent system operator/power exchange) in time for their launch next Janaury," she added.
An independent system operator will be responsible under California law for operating the interconnected transmission system.
